In parallel, QurAlis is preparing to advance QRL-201 into a pivotal clinical trial (CONQUR) in the first half of 2027. * * ###### November 16, 2026 # QurAlis Receives FDA Clearance for IND Application of QRL-201 for the Treatment of ALS, Clearing a Path to Initiation of Pivotal Clinical Trial in the U.S. Company also announces final data from the ANQUR clinical trial DRF phase that demonstrated QRL-201 slowed disease progression as measured by ALSFRS-R by 50 percent (p<0.05), and showed statistically significant reductions in NfL and pNfH, biomarkers of axonal damage in ALS QurAlis plans to initiate a pivotal study in the first half of 2027; ANQUR open-label extended dosing is ongoing in Canada, the UK, and the EU CAMBRIDGE, Mass., November 16, 2026 – QurAlis Corporation (“QurAlis”), today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has cleared its Investigational New Drug (IND) application for QRL-201 for the treatment of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). The clearance enables QurAlis to advance the planned pivotal CONQUR clinical trial in the U.S.  The company also announced final data from the dose-range finding (DRF) phase of its Proof-of-Concept Phase 1/2 ANQUR clinical trial of QRL-201 in people living with ALS that demonstrated QRL-201 effectively slowed disease progression by 50 percent (p<0.05).  * Treatment of QRL-201 was associated with a statistically significant reduction from baseline of 46 percent in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) phosphorylated neurofilament heavy (pNfH) in the 3mg QRL-201 group at Day 197, the last timepoint measured (p<0.01); pNfH serves as a clinically relevant biomarker of axonal damage.  * QRL-201 demonstrated statistically significant decreases in plasma neurofilament light (NfL), with reductions of 18% from baseline (p<0.01) and 31% versus placebo (p=0.07) in the 3 mg group at Day 337 and 36% from baseline (p=0.01) in the 10mg group at Day 421. The reductions in NfL observed bring NfL levels in both QRL-201 dose groups to approximately 1.4-fold-to-1.7-fold of those observed in healthy individuals, similar to absolute levels observed in clinical trials with other genetically targeted ALS treatments for certain familial sub-populations. * QRL-201 was generally safe and well tolerated across all phases of the ANQUR study, with most adverse events reported as mild or moderate and no serious adverse events have been reported in the DRF phase of the study.  The ANQUR study has now fully transitioned into the open-label extended (OLE) dosing phase and is in progress in Canada, the United Kingdom (UK), and the European Union (EU). In parallel, QurAlis is preparing to advance QRL-201 into a pivotal clinical trial (CONQUR) in the first half of 2027. Additional information about the CONQUR clinical trial will be forthcoming in early 2027. About STATHMIN-2 STATHMIN-2 (STMN2) is a well-validated protein important for neural repair, axonal stability, and muscle innervation and is the most significantly regulated gene by TDP-43 exclusively in humans. STMN2 has the most consistently decreased expression across multiple ALS RNA expression studies. Loss of nuclear TDP-43 leads to mis-splicing of the pre-mRNA of STMN2. This mis-splicing results in a loss of full-length transcript and protein. QRL-201 rescues STMN2 loss of function and neurodegenerative phenotypes in QurAlis’ ALS patient-derived motor neuron disease models in the presence of TDP-43 pathology. TDP-43 pathology is associated with nearly all ALS patients, approximately 50 percent of patients with frontotemporal dementia (FTD), the second most common form of dementia, and with about a third of Alzheimer’s Disease patients. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Advancing precision neuroscience pipeline across multiple clinical and preclinical programs (https://www.quralis.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/QurAlis-Corporate-Presentation-March-2026.pdf) citeturn516search12 [wordlim: 200] Published: 8 months ago; Crawled: 7 months ago; QRL-201 ...
